children: By Darshan Kumar R

London's blue-chip stocks closed at a seven-week high on Thursday after the finance minister reaffirmed the government's commitment to fiscal discipline, while a shift into defensive sectors amid a deepening global selloff in AI-related stocks also supported the benchmark.
The benchmark FTSE 100 index
CURRENCYCOM:UK100
closed higher by 1.1% to 10,840.35 points, its highest since August 26, while the midcap FTSE 250
also rose 0.26%.
Investors sought refuge in defensive sectors as a global chip stocks selloff intensified, benefiting UK's large caps with limited exposure to AI

"It's a rotation towards long-term; almost an infrastructure play without the risk of a rate increase and healthcare, consumer cyclicals are a safer heaven as they are not overly leveraged," said Nick Saunders, CEO of Webull UK
Drugmakers AstraZeneca
and GSK
climbed 3.2% and 2.9%, respectively
Dove soap maker Unilever
rose 1.8% and cigarette maker British American Tobacco
advanced 2.5%
British finance minister John Healey said this month's budget would aim at bolstering economic resilience, adding that he and Prime Minister Andy Burnham were aligned on maintaining fiscal discipline
Financials (.FTNMX301010), including heavily weighted banks, was up 0.3%
UK's gross domestic product rose 0.1% in August, boosted by AI optimism, against expectations of a 0.1% drop
Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said that any future interest rate increase should not be interpreted by investors as the start of a prolonged series of rate hikes
Economists polled by Reuters expect the BoE to raise rates to 4% in November
Industrial metal miners (.FTNMX551020) were down 1.4%, on weaker copper prices
Antofagasta
fell 4.1%, after the Chilean miner's third-quarter copper production declined year-on-year
E-commerce group THG
surged 16.3% after lifting its annual profit forecast
Paper and packaging firm Mondi
slumped 7.9% after hiking prices for several paper grades to offset higher energy costs

title: UK's FTSE 100 closes at seven-week high on fiscal reassurance, defensive buying
